title: Address to the most pious ladies
english: An address to the most pious ladies.

I would call you an honor for the whole world, and the pride of the holy churches of Christ our common Savior — his brides, most pious and God-loved queens. The many-colored beauty of virtue flashes on you, a beauty sweet and plain to the eyes of the Godhead. Study and zeal have already brought it to pass. What remains is to shine by a right faith that nothing shakes.

Somewhere the wise Paul writes — truly learned in the law, and the one who served as priest of Christ’s mystery among the nations — “Therefore, my beloved brothers, be steadfast, immovable, always abounding in the work of the Lord.”
For where right and spotless faith keeps step with the boasts that come from good works, and the two enter on equal footing,

title: Praise deferred; virgin courts and temples
english: there you will find perfection in every good thing, and what stands sound for holiness.
So every word we have trails behind the renown that is already yours, and admits defeat without a blush. It may even deserve pardon if it fears to praise what it cannot reach.

If speech could do what it longs to do, it would stand charged with weakness for delaying. No one should clear that delay by calling it laziness. Why wound people you could have adorned with praise of virtue, by choosing silence instead?

But if speech goes slack, fears, and admits defeat, we will not blame it so much as you — you who are so public that the surpassing weight of your own brave acts has made even the speeches that usually dress everyone look like nothing.

Royal blood has come down to you from long ago, and it still runs, as we believe. Yet look: you also take hold of the kingship in Christ, and you are eager to think and to do what pleases him — shining by works and by a faith without blame, brightening your courts and the emperors’ with the glory of virginity, and raising costly temples to Christ.
He has given this too, with the rest, to your holy souls.
So I will take a word from the holy writings: “Rejoice in the Lord always; again I will say, rejoice. Let your fairness be known to all people.”
It is known, then, and cried abroad even to those throughout

title: Gift of the booklet; creed begins
english: every land and city — like an image that carries the beauty of piety toward Christ in its drawing — it has shone out clearly and been judged worthy of every wonder.

I thought I ought also to hand a spiritual gift to women already sound toward every good, as to holy brides of Christ: this little book I have freshly worked. It can give no small help, I think, to those who will read it.

Those taught — or rather talked into — wrong thoughts about Christ our common Savior it will lead back and initiate well. Those who already walk with a right mind and dwell in the doctrines of the truth it will make safer still, by many findings from good thoughts and by proofs from the God-breathed Scripture.
For the reader will learn that Emmanuel is God by nature and in truth, and that because of him the virgin who bore him is God-bearer.
Those who fear both to say this and to think it have not grasped, as one would expect, how deep the mystery of piety is.

I take it I must say in brief the apostolic and gospel tradition made concerning Christ the master of all, the aim of all God-breathed Scripture upon him, and wherever the force of the doctrines of the truth looks.

We believe, then, in one God, the Father almighty, maker of all things visible and invisible; and in one Lord, Jesus the Christ, his Son, begotten by nature from him before every age and time. title: Trinity; Word made flesh; Theotokos
english: hypostasis. We likewise believe in the Holy Spirit, not counting him a stranger to the divine nature; for he is poured out from the Father by nature through the Son upon creation.
So the holy and worshiped Trinity is understood as one, same in substance, and one in the identity of glory.

We say that this same Only-begotten Word, begotten beyond speech from the substance of God the Father, maker of the ages, the one through whom and in whom all things are, the true light, the nature that gives life to all — for he has appeared as life from the Father’s life — in the last times of the age, when the Father was pleased to save the race on earth that had fallen under a curse and been brought down by sin into death and decay, took hold of Abraham’s seed, as the Scriptures say, shared blood and flesh — that is, became human — and taking flesh and making it his own, was born in the flesh through the holy God-bearer Mary.

Yet though he became as we are and put on the slave’s form by the plan of the economy, he remained in the deity and lordship that are his by nature. He did not stop being God when he became flesh — that is, when he became as we are, a human. Because he is unchangeable by nature as God, remaining what he always was and is and will be, he has also been named Son of Man.

And since he came down willingly into the measures of humanity — for he lowered himself into emptying — he also had to endure birth from a woman. His divine nature did not take a beginning of being when he is said to have been born according to the flesh. He was, and is, as I said, the Word from God the Father by nature and in truth.
